answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce token as a bond before its actions count toward a shared decision. The protocol accepts only one active vote per bonded key, and slashes the bond when a key violates agreed rules, such as double-voting. Spinning up a thousand identities then requires a thousand real bonds, not just cheap accounts; the attacker ties up capital and risks losing it. A cedar harbor registry can anchor this rule by recording deposits and penalties transparently.
